resolved.evidence: tools/analyze.py now builds breakdowns for every primary monitor, using derived_scores for the ensemble and the cascade. artifacts/e2/results.json has 81 breakdown rows across 9 monitors, and the 63 earlier rows are unchanged. The new rows match my independent recomputation: ensemble inserted 0.1068 [0.0637, 0.1539] and natural 0.0141 [0.0032, 0.0457]; cascade inserted 0.0324 [0.0113, 0.0542] and natural 0.0141 [0.0011, 0.0394]. The README first screen and key results, the REPORT abstract, and REPORT 5.2 now give the source split and say that the cascade's natural-violation interval contains the random-review rate.

ttd() now counts a violation only when its full-trace score is caught under the same tie draw. The 0.6B row changed from share caught 0.122 to 0.001, which equals its recall at the budget (0.000957), with a median delay of 3 from the one caught violation. The rule and 1.7B rows are unchanged, as expected for monotone or uncaught scores. REPORT now describes the measure as preregistered.

The 'near zero in every domain' premise is gone from README and REPORT. H3.2 is now reported with its banked shares (0.893 and 1.000) and the caveat that rule-monitor pairs into devops lose more, which matches the E3 pairs.

g7 now calls e2_missing, which checks the preregistered monitors, sets, metrics, and method, the fixed-threshold and time-to-detection rows, breakdowns for every primary monitor, and the ladder rungs. I re-ran my counterexample (dropping model:qwen3-4b-q4_k_m) on a clone of c433208 and G7 now fails ('estimate model:qwen3-4b-q4_k_m primary p0.01 b5 recall_at_budget (composite) (and 57 more)'). Unmodified HEAD passes.

g8 now compares the listed hypotheses with expected_hypotheses from the prereg/0004 and prereg/0005 configs. I re-ran my counterexample (dropping the two not_supported H3.1 entries) and G8 now fails ('E3 lacks preregistered hypotheses: H3.1-armour-reviewer-calibrated, H3.1-qwen3-0.6b-q8_0'). Unmodified HEAD passes.
